levers.name: TTC service standards
levers.summary: The TTC is a City of Toronto service agency, governed by a Board with decision-making authority delegated by City Council. Its Board-approved service standards guide how often routes run, how crowded vehicles get, and what counts as an on-time departure.

standards.frequency: During the weekday morning peak, the minimum service level for local bus routes is every 30 minutes or better.
standards.reliability: A surface vehicle counts as an on-time departure if it leaves its origin timepoint between 1 minute early and 5 minutes late.
standards.review: The TTC is reviewing its service standards, with a report back to its Board scheduled for Q4 2026.

sources.title: City of Toronto: Agencies (TTC listed as a Service Agency)
sources.supports: TTC manages and operates the City's subways, streetcars, buses and Wheel-Trans; service agencies are governed by a Board with delegated decision-making authority from City Council (page modified 2025-12-04).

sources.title: TTC report: Overview of TTC Service Standards (Strategic Planning Committee, September 4, 2025)
sources.supports: Board-approved service standards are applied at every level of TTC service planning; example standards for peak frequency, vehicle crowding and on-time departures; review to report back in Q4 2026.

levers.name: RentSafeTO and the indoor temperature bylaw
levers.summary: The City asks tenants to make repair requests in writing, sets landlord response times (24 hours urgent, seven days non-urgent), takes complaints through 311, and requires at least 21°C from October 1 to May 15 where the landlord pays for heat.

sources.title: City of Toronto: RentSafeTO for tenants: service requests
sources.supports: Requests in writing, keep a copy; 24-hour urgent and seven-day non-urgent response; 311 if unresolved (page modified 2026-02-24).

sources.title: City of Toronto: Indoor temperatures in apartment units
sources.supports: 21°C minimum October 1 to May 15 where the owner pays for heat; 311 if unresolved (page modified 2026-09-01).

levers.name: Ontario rent increase guideline
levers.summary: How much most tenants' rent can rise each year is set by the Province of Ontario's rent increase guideline (2.1% for 2026), not by City Council. Units first occupied for residential purposes after November 15, 2018 are exempt from rent control.

sources.title: Government of Ontario: Residential rent increases
sources.supports: 2026 guideline 2.1%; maximum most tenants' rent can rise without Landlord and Tenant Board approval; post-November 15, 2018 units exempt (page updated 2026-06-23).
